resources.string: Live WHOOP heart rate on your home screen

1. In the WHOOP app, open your device settings and turn on "Heart Rate Broadcast".
2. Grant Bluetooth and notification permissions when asked.
3. Tap "Start streaming", then add the RawPulse widgets to your home screen (long-press home screen → Widgets → RawPulse).

Note: while RawPulse is connected, your WHOOP can’t also broadcast to another device (Peloton, Zwift, etc.) at the same time.
Unofficial. Not affiliated with or endorsed by WHOOP.

The HRV shown here is a live RMSSD measured from your WHOOP\'s beat-to-beat data over the last minute, so it moves with your breathing and activity in real time. The WHOOP app instead reports a single HRV measured during deep sleep and averaged across the night. Different windows, different methods — the numbers will not match, and that\'s expected. Use this for live trends, not as a replacement for WHOOP\'s recovery figure.
Bluetooth permission is required to read your WHOOP heart-rate broadcast.
Your heart rate straight off your WHOOP, updating beat by beat. The number you can glance at mid-workout without opening a single app.

Heart-rate variability (RMSSD), measured live from your beat-to-beat data over the last minute. It rises when you\'re calm and settles under strain — a real-time window the WHOOP app only shows you after you sleep.
How hard you\'re working, as a percentage of your max heart rate. Colour-coded from rest to all-out (zones 0–5), so one glance tells you whether you\'re cruising or redlining.
A running summary of your current session — lowest, average and highest heart rate, plus elapsed time. The whole workout\'s story in one tile.

I built RawPulse solo — no company, no team, just me making an app I use every day.

There's no dashboard, no data collection, no tracking. Your heart rate stays on your device, not on some server.
